messages.subject: INLA models across different spatial scales
parts:
Morning,

  My name is Ara. I am PhD student at the University of New Mexico working on a global marine predator project. I was wondering if anyone has looked at how INLA behaves at different spatial scales. Currently I have a global grid at 880km2 and 110km2. We suspect that certain predictor variables will change as we change grid sizes but we are seeing some weirdness. 

I am running R 3.2.4 (2016-03-10) and INLA 0.0.1455098891

ISSUE
At 880km2 grid the INLA gives us a slope of -0.0433 for temperature. This is close to what our not corrected for spatial autocorrelation theory predicts. But at 110km2  grid we get 0.02 slope for temperature while the glm gives us (-0.42) something close to theory. For richness data (counts of species) we run through a similar model, just predicting richness. We see predictor variables moving around like we would expect for no odd behavior. I know as grid sizes get smaller spatial autocorrelation tends to go up. But in another dataset I am using I work at 10km2 grids and we have no problems. 

I was wondering if anyone had some ideas as to what is going on and if there is a fix. 

880km2 MODELS
GLM
Call:  glm(formula = logopCon ~ lognppvgmp + tempannual + logbathy + 
    logcstlen + logprox, family = gaussian, data = richness.df, 
    na.action = na.exclude)

The full INLA setup is:
rich_map$idx <- 1:nrow(rich_map)

form <- logopCon ~ annualtemp + lognppvgmp + logbath + logcstlen + logprox +
  f(idx, model = "besag", graph = adj)

           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

DATA PROCESSING
We gathered rasters and point data from a range of sources. lognppvgmp is a raster with 1 km resolution, annualtemp is a raster with 4 km resolution, logbath is from the ETOPO1 dataset, logopCon is consumption data on a grid.

For the lognppvgmp, annualtemp, logbath, and logprox rasters we did a mean value per grid cell. So at a give scale 880km2 or 110km2 there are different values. The logcstlen is just the coastline length for a given cell, again this changes with grid size. logopCon is the odd one, in that's it's point data and I did a Point in Polygon sum to get at all the consumption in a given grid.

Thanks!
ara

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA models across different spatial scales
parts:
Hi Anna,

The problem with the Beasg (or ICAR(1)) model is that it doesn't behave consistently under refinement.  This means that you are comparing estimates from *very* different models!

There is also the issue that the model is ``unscaled'', which means that the ``precision parameter'' actually means quite different things between the models.  As the same priors are being used, this can lead to accidentally very informative priors.

For the first issue (Besag not behaving consistently under discretisation), I would recommend changing to SPDE priors.

For the second issue (i.e. if you want to stick with something like a Besag model), you can do some scaling.  The easiest version is to replace "model = "besag"" with "model = "bym2"".  This will also add an i.i.d. random effect in each cell.  If you'd rather turn it off and get the pure Besag model, you can use the following:


  f(idx, model = "bym2", graph = adj, hyper = list(phi=list(intial=15, fixed=TRUE) ) )

which fixes the mixing parameter phi to be approximately 1 (prior is on the logit scale), which corresponds to the Besag model.  Details can be found in this paper: http://arxiv.org/pdf/1601.01180.pdf

Fixing the scaling may be enough to fix the problem, but it may not be...

Hope this helps!

Dan

The full INLA setup is:
rich_map$idx <- 1:nrow(rich_map)

form <- logopCon ~ annualtemp + lognppvgmp + logbath + logcstlen + logprox +
  f(idx, model = "besag", graph = adj)

trdf <- as.data.frame(rich_map)

m1 <- inla(form, data = trdf, family="gaussian" ,control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

DATA PROCESSING
We gathered rasters and point data from a range of sources. lognppvgmp is a raster with 1 km resolution, annualtemp is a raster with 4 km resolution, logbath is from the ETOPO1 dataset, logopCon is consumption data on a grid.

For the lognppvgmp, annualtemp, logbath, and logprox rasters we did a mean value per grid cell. So at a give scale 880km2 or 110km2 there are different values. The logcstlen is just the coastline length for a given cell, again this changes with grid size. logopCon is the odd one, in that's it's point data and I did a Point in Polygon sum to get at all the consumption in a given grid.

Thanks!
